channel.title: The African Street Journal
channel.description: Daily news from all 55 African countries, every source cited.

item.title: Sierra Leone charcoal trade cuts trees as clean-cooking access stays low
item.description: The government’s National Energy Compact says only 15% of the population has access to clean cooking, while charcoal supports some families’ livelihoods.

item.title: Sierra Leone debate questions whether vice president can succeed president
item.description: An analysis argues that past officeholders lacked a clear route to succession, citing Solomon Berewa’s 2007 defeat as the SLPP candidate.

item.title: Senegal federation challenges Morocco’s awarded Africa Cup title at sports court
item.description: The African football confederation gave Morocco a 3-0 forfeit win after Senegal had beaten it 1-0 in the 18 January final.

item.title: Mauritanian police seize 1,7 tonne of cocaine near Mali border
item.description: The haul was intercepted in eastern Mauritania after three months of intelligence work; police also arrested two foreign nationals suspected of involvement.

item.title: Rwandan scholar wins South Africa's Best Doctoral Student award
item.description: Dr. Claudine Nkeragutabara Ndimurukundo received the honour at the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research's 2026 awards.

item.title: Nigerian banks look to cut diesel costs to keep services running
item.description: Power interruptions can halt transactions, and banks are seeking ways to reduce their reliance on diesel generators.

item.title: Kenya's election commission will follow court rules on 2027 results
item.description: Chairperson Erastus Ethekon says the commission will tally and verify results collectively, while only he can declare the winner.

item.title: Diffa governor explains Niger’s decision to expel Mohamid community
item.description: Mahamadou Ibrahim Bagadoma distinguished the group from Nigerien Arabs and urged clear communication to protect social cohesion.

item.title: Mozambican health official Samo Gudo elected to lead 112-country public health body
item.description: Gudo, director of the National Institute of Health, becomes the first African to hold the presidency of the International Association of National Public Health Institutes.

item.title: Congo faces Guinea in March for spot at U23 Africa Cup of Nations finals
item.description: The Diables Rouges must beat the Guinean Olympic selection in a two-legged tie starting at home on March 22.

item.title: Equatorial Guinea and France examine cultural and French-teaching proposals
item.description: At a meeting in Mongomo, officials discussed training cultural workers, teaching French and improving preparation for French teachers.

item.title: Angolan consulate and youth entrepreneurs agree to plan financial-literacy content for...
item.description: The two sides will first draft a 10-topic plan on running businesses in the United Kingdom before the content begins to publish.

item.title: Tunisia rises to 61st in English ranking as score falls eight points
item.description: The 2026 index puts Tunisia above the global average, but still in the low-proficiency category, with a 71-point gap between Ariana and Sidi Bouzid.

item.title: Insecurity disrupts classes for 3 979 children in Mali
item.description: The UNICEF figure covers pupils affected by the crisis, while 639 students displaced from Kidal were counted in Gao after April 2026 violence.

item.title: Guinea’s bauxite company seeks samplers for Kamsar site
item.description: The hires would collect and prepare bauxite samples, measure moisture and grain size, and send results to engineers and operators.

item.title: Southern African Parliamentary Forum tables E72.14 million budget for 2027/28
item.description: The proposed budget was presented to the 59th Plenary Assembly, which Eswatini hosted, as member parliaments debate the body's financial sustainability.

item.title: Tanzania’s finance minister joins Paris forum on African debt
item.description: Khamis Mussa Omar will join a session on access to affordable, sustainable debt as African governments face rising debt-service obligations.

item.title: Mali's health and higher-education ministries welcome 19 new medical and pharmacy lectu...
item.description: The 19 Malians passed the aggregation exam of the African and Malagasy Council for Higher Education (CAMES), out of 23 candidates presented.

item.title: Eswatini urges schools to keep pregnant pupils in education
item.description: Senator Linda Nxumalo says schools must prevent stigma and discrimination and support teenage mothers returning to class under the national policy.

item.title: Libyan-British forum agrees exploratory business visit to Libya
item.description: The London meeting also discussed UK registration support for Libyan firms and British investment in an aluminium project with a Libyan partner.

item.title: Togo closes mosque and extends church suspension over noise complaints
item.description: The government says the measures enforce limits of 70 decibels by day and 55 at night under a 2025 order.

item.title: Harare court issues arrest warrant for Chatunga Mugabe after no-show
item.description: The youngest son of Zimbabwe's former president missed a routine remand hearing in a robbery and property-damage case.

item.title: Pharmacists seek freeze on 50-dinar medicine order fee
item.description: Tunisia’s pharmacy union wants the charge suspended until the health minister makes a clear, final decision on its legal basis.

item.title: Congo employers urge tax changes in 2027 budget review
item.description: UniCongo asked lawmakers to tax company income rather than turnover and revise rules on penalties, registration fees, VAT and payroll tax.

item.title: Moroccan tomato exports push European prices down to €1.10 per kilogram
item.description: Prices fell from €1.80 to €2 per kilogram as slower sales pressured traders to discount their produce.

item.title: Egypt’s deputy prime minister puts social protection at centre of economic stability
item.description: Hussein Issa told the opening of Egypt’s first International Social Protection Forum that safety nets can support demand and protect human capital.

item.title: Mombasa port fire kills two as investigation begins
item.description: The Kenya Ports Authority says a gas cylinder explosion ignited a kiosk fire outside the port on Monday, and crews stopped it spreading.

item.title: Kenya plans 6.16 million fruit seedlings for 2027/28
item.description: The draft budget policy includes date palms for growers in arid and semi-arid areas, alongside seedlings for eight other crops.

item.title: Tanzania releases 19 billion/- for Arusha road compensation
item.description: The works minister ordered the roads agency to pay eligible residents within two to three days and told contractors to speed up construction.

item.title: Peace torch visit shuts Bubanza market for most of a day
item.description: Traders reopened at 16 h 30, while schools in the town’s commercial centre closed so pupils and teachers could attend the reception.

item.title: CIPRES trains social-protection officials in new management tools
item.description: About a hundred officials are attending the 23-27 November seminar in Abidjan, which aims to spread revised accounting and pension-management rules.

item.title: Burundi’s refugee agency orders urban return ahead of surprise camp checks
item.description: ONPRA representatives demanded formal identification from hundreds of city-dwelling refugees, threatening loss of status for those absent during verification.

item.title: Mozambique deepens rice technology deal with Chinese firm Wanbao
item.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, Environment and Fisheries and Wanbao are expanding the transfer of rice cultivation technology, with the stated aim of boosting domestic production.

item.title: Morocco plans annual imports of 30,000 cows to rebuild herds
item.description: Agriculture Minister Khalid Hatimy said the six-year programme would also support local breeding and investment in feedlots and dairy production.

item.title: Somalia’s speaker accuses Kenya, Ethiopia and Uganda of colluding with Al-Shabaab
item.description: Abdulkadir Mohamed Nur alleges Israel has assembled the countries, the militants and forces loyal to a former regional leader against Mogadishu.

item.title: Cameroon rights commission urges equal treatment for election candidates
item.description: The commission cited document delays, refusals and fees as candidates prepared for legislative and municipal elections on 07 February 2027.

item.title: Obiang meets Evinayong bishop ahead of diocesan celebration
item.description: The president and Bishop Calixto Paulino discussed the diocese, whose patronal celebration is scheduled for 27 November.

item.title: Burundi residents demand independent inquiry into police chief's river death
item.description: Police in Bugendana say Sébastien Niragira killed himself, but residents of Jenda hill dispute that account and are seeking an independent investigation.

item.title: Mauritius leaves femicide and marital-rape reforms unproclaimed
item.description: Parliament passed the Criminal Code changes in July, but they cannot take effect until they are formally proclaimed.

item.title: Niger presents 50 projects to investors at Niamey forum
item.description: The three-day event has drawn 300 investors from 30 countries and targets agreements worth CFA5,500 billion.

item.title: Most Rwandan consumers targeted by digital fraud, TransUnion survey finds
item.description: Money and gift card scams were the most reported schemes, while fears of identity misuse topped consumers' concerns.

item.title: Eswatini volleyball chief joins global congress that approves new rules
item.description: The International Volleyball Federation approved a new constitution and rules for indoor and beach volleyball at its 40th World Congress in the Dominican Republic.

item.title: Ivory Coast health chief says families owe nothing to receive stillborn babies
item.description: Dr Kouakoussui Konan Lambert says hospitals will notify police before transferring each body to the morgue and funeral services.

item.title: Morocco and Madagascar sign nine cooperation agreements in Rabat
item.description: The countries also backed Morocco’s autonomy plan, while Rabat will raise scholarship places for Malagasy students from 90 to 200.

item.title: Diffa governor conveys president’s message at Tandja remembrance
item.description: Authorities and residents gathered in Mainé-Soroa for prayers marking six years since the former Nigerien president’s death.

item.title: Tunisia plans marriage preparation programme and family mediation body
item.description: The family ministry will coordinate training with three ministries and prepare a bill to create an institution for resolving marital disputes.

item.title: Rokel community calls for inquiry into Container Junction crashes
item.description: Stakeholders say the junction on the Freetown-Waterloo Highway has recorded several fatal incidents over the years, and they want signs and no-parking zones installed.

item.title: South Sudan welcomes new IGAD treaty as it takes effect
item.description: The 2023 treaty replaces the 1996 agreement and sets a stronger legal and institutional framework for the regional organisation.

item.title: Equatorial Guinea’s vice-president begins Egypt visit
item.description: Teodoro Nguema Obiang Mangue is due to meet President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi and other officials to discuss cooperation between the countries.

item.title: Edgars leans on Carousel factories to drive growth
item.description: The Zimbabwean clothing retailer plans closer ties between manufacturing and retail to control costs, quality and stock supply.

item.title: Bangui's 6th arrondissement mayor reviews first 100 days in office
item.description: Crépin Ngoko-Nzengue outlined actions already under way and his plans to improve the arrondissement's organisation and development.

item.title: Zenith suspends $573 million arbitration against Tunisia
item.description: The energy group says its British subsidiaries will stop advancing Tunisia’s unpaid share of the arbitration costs, delaying a final ruling.

item.title: Libya’s Audit Bureau reports 2025 deficit of 5,385,015,697 dinars
item.description: The 19-chapter report puts revenue at 165,683,644,617 dinars and expenditure at 171,068,660,314 dinars.

item.title: Togo lists eight warning signs of fraudulent investment firms
item.description: A consumer warning urges savers to check authorization with the relevant regulator, after subscribers to the company CBC found its offices closed.

item.title: Doumbouya appoints 38 senior officials to Guinea’s health ministry
item.description: The appointments cover public health oversight, hospitals, nutrition, laboratories and the fight against disease.

item.title: Cape Verde team presents parasite test in Chile, with Portugal trial ahead
item.description: The Bioanalítica and University Jean Piaget reagent has been used in schistosomiasis outbreaks in Cape Verde and Mozambique.

item.title: Musasizi urges banks to cut lending rates as profits reach USh2.17 trillion
item.description: The finance minister says private-sector credit must rise from 14% of GDP to 25% by 2030 to support Uganda’s US$500 billion economy ambition.

item.title: Mauritius charges man after brother’s death in Saint-Julien-d’Hotman
item.description: A court sent Selven Kistnasamy back to custody after he was charged with assault causing bodily harm without intent to kill.

item.title: Chad proposes 3 CFA070 billion budget for 2027
item.description: Finance Minister Tahir Hamid Nguilin projects resources up 35% and spending up 19%, with oil receipts forecast to rise despite lower output.

item.title: Zimbabwe's nurses accuse government of cutting health budget share
item.description: The Zimbabwe Nurses Association says the proposed 2027 allocation falls further below the 15% target set by the Abuja Declaration.

item.title: Delta police investigate campaign clash as curfew covers Ughelli North
item.description: Police report six deaths and several injuries at a campaign event, while the state government restricts movement overnight across the local government area.

item.title: Army clashes with the Patriotic Resistance Coalition in Djugu drive displaced people to...
item.description: Renewed fighting in Ituri province is worsening security in Djugu territory and pushing people out of the area toward the provincial capital.

item.title: Mauritius inflation reaches 6.4% as central bank raises rate to 5.00%
item.description: CareEdge Africa says October’s annual inflation was the highest this year, while higher rates will raise household loan repayments and constrain business plans.

item.title: Stanbic commits US$75,000 to children's hernia surgeries
item.description: The three-year pledge will support free operations by Celebration Health, after the bank increased its annual contribution from US$15,000 to US$25,000.

item.title: Qualikeeper wins Qualcomm's US$75,000 livestock technology grant
item.description: The Ghanaian company will use the equity-free award and technical support to develop and expand its livestock intelligence platform.

item.title: Sao Tome police detain four over suspected illegal sand extraction
item.description: The law requires a licence or authorisation to remove sand, with environmental compensation and possible criminal liability also at issue.

item.title: São Tomé plans solar mini-grids for three isolated communities
item.description: The project will add or improve solar power with battery storage, while officials prepare a tariff model for the future systems.

item.title: Liberia’s fertilizer shortages squeeze small farmers’ harvests
item.description: Farmers say higher prices linked to the US-Israeli war with Iran are making supplies unaffordable, while a proposed deal with OCP Africa remains unsigned.

item.title: Equatorial Guinea approves 15 economic and institutional initiatives
item.description: The measures include a 2027-2031 youth employment plan, fuel reserves, electricity rules and new trade and maritime service windows.

item.title: Malawi starts K131 billion upgrade of 31-kilometre Chitipa-Ilomba road
item.description: The bitumen-standard project is due to take 24 months and is intended to improve access to markets and cut transport costs.

item.title: First Capital Bank Botswana backs men's health run with P50,000
item.description: The sponsorship is part of the bank's Movember campaign, which aims to get men talking about their health and wellbeing.

item.title: Liberia lawmakers test credibility of FY2027 revenue estimates
item.description: A House committee hearing will examine collection performance, tax exemptions and the capacity of institutions that raise domestic revenue.

item.title: Senegal PM proposes statistics fund as harvest data gaps hinder sales
item.description: Ahmadou Al Aminou Lô says missing production totals leave crop sellers without reliable market guides and make banks struggle to assess farmers’ needs.

item.title: Lusaka court gives Kang’ombe five days to pay K100,000
item.description: The former lawmaker was ordered to account for Binwell Mpundu’s continued absence from court, where Mpundu faces a seditious practices charge.

item.title: Somalia's prime minister replaces defence minister with Saadaq Joon
item.description: The appointment comes as the country prepares for a security handover and the African Union mission's mandate expires on 31 December.

item.title: Sierra Leone Judiciary seeks public help to locate murder case accused
item.description: The bench warrant for Mohamed Haroun Conteh remains in force after the accused reportedly failed to return to custody during a 2023 prison break.

item.title: Sam-Ouandja hospital imposes daily charges on inpatients
item.description: A Central African Republic report also records allegations that an elderly woman died after being left without sufficient care in her bed.

item.title: Togo’s business formalities centre handles company registration
item.description: The CFE issues a trade-register entry and tax identification number after founders submit documents that vary with their chosen legal structure.

item.title: Abuja court freezes N135.5 billion tied to Governors’ Forum
item.description: The order bars the forum and 29 banks from moving the funds while the court considers a lawyer’s claim under a 2018 indemnity.

item.title: Benin court sentences former police chief Houndégnon to 24 months
item.description: The former director was convicted over online harassment and incitement to rebellion linked to his criticism of reforms under Patrice Talon.

item.title: Guinea prosecutors seek 10 years for two police officers in theft case
item.description: The prosecution also wants each of the two officers to pay a 5 million Guinean franc fine, with a ruling due on 30 November.

item.title: Namibia’s mining sector faces an electricity constraint on growth
item.description: The industry accounted for 53% of export earnings and 14% of GDP in 2025, while using nearly a quarter of domestic electricity.

item.title: Chidale defends Malawi Open title and wins $5 000
item.description: The Malawian golfer beat a field that included 35 foreign players at the four-day tournament in Lilongwe.

item.title: Liberia drug agency chief-designate plans overhaul affecting 1,400 volunteers
item.description: Daniel Dee Ziankahn Jr. told senators the reforms would begin at headquarters before extending to satellite stations nationwide.

item.title: Chad signs $25 million local-governance deal with Switzerland and the UN's development...
item.description: The project aims to build the capacity of local authorities and bring administration closer to citizens.

item.title: Police send woman to Dakar prosecutor over alleged extortion
item.description: A Grand-Dakar shopkeeper said she threatened to accuse him of attempted rape after he refused a second request for transport money.

item.title: Mauritius targets 25 000 arpents under crops
item.description: The Food Security Programme 2026-2030 is due to launch in two weeks and aims to help cut food import dependence.

item.title: RSF and Tasis announce capture of Bau headquarters in Blue Nile
item.description: Their 20 November claim covers Bau Locality and Village 12, while Sudan’s army says it repelled an attack at Dering.

item.title: Museveni meets Uganda’s ICC judicial candidate
item.description: Rosette Muzigo-Morrison, a lawyer with more than 30 years in international criminal law and human rights, is Uganda’s candidate for the 2026 elections.

item.title: Botswana reopens debate on recognising plural marriage
item.description: A proposal raised in Ntlo ya Dikgosi has renewed questions about whether the law should recognise men having more than one wife.

item.title: Human rights commission gives education department 60 days to act on school crisis
item.description: The commission cited overcrowding, unsafe buildings and sanitation failures in public schools, with its report recording classes of up to 101 learners.

item.title: Liberia finance ministry defends US$1.54 billion budget forecast
item.description: Deputy Finance Minister Anthony G. Myers says recurring revenue and new tax measures will support the FY2027 plan despite concerns over shortfalls.

item.title: Azande king urges South Sudanese to register for elections
item.description: Atoroba Peni Rikito Gbudue registered in Yambio and called on citizens to choose leaders through elections rather than armed conflict.

item.title: South Sudanese youth urge government to expand jobs and political voice
item.description: After a six-day visit to Senegal for the 2026 Youth Olympic Games, Deng Wiyual Nyang called for investment in young people at home.

item.title: Ghana's Black Challenge to bring home first amputee football World Cup
item.description: The squad flies back to Accra on November 26 after a 1-0 final win over Morocco in Mexico.

item.title: Algeria advances $14.6 billion railway to Tamanrasset
item.description: The route is planned to carry passengers and freight, with the full line scheduled for delivery by the end of 2028.

item.title: Illovo commits $12 million to Malawi smallholder sugar scheme
item.description: The Kazilira project covers 308 hectares at Dwangwa and is expected to add 4 500 metric tonnes of sugar each year.

item.title: Party seeks written answer from Namibia's electoral commission on N$2.2m vehicle
item.description: The party wants the commission to say whether its former chairperson received the vehicle and under what rule it was assigned.

item.title: Botswana's non-diamond economy grows 1.6% as private credit shrinks
item.description: Diamond output swings lifted quarterly growth to 8.7%, while the private sector that supplies almost two-thirds of output expanded far more slowly.

item.title: Mahrez rules out return to Algeria's national team
item.description: The former captain says the younger squad must be allowed to learn from hard results after the World Cup exit and the Togo defeat.
